short: The flagship of the French Navy and the only non-American nuclear-powered aircraft carrier.
full:
Commissioned on 18 May 2001, the French aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle (R91) is the flagship of the Marine Nationale. It holds the distinction of being the first French nuclear-powered surface vessel and the only nuclear-powered aircraft carrier completed by a nation other than the United States. Capable of operating a catapult-assisted take-off but arrested recovery (CATOBAR) system, it deploys a formidable air group primarily comprising Dassault Rafale M multirole fighters.

The Charles de Gaulle provides France with an independent global strike capability and a powerful tool for maritime diplomacy. It has seen extensive operational deployment, supporting NATO operations in Afghanistan and playing a central role in military strikes against the Islamic State in the Middle East. Despite early technical teething problems, it has proven to be an exceptionally capable platform and remains a cornerstone of European naval power.
